ei.title: Chemistry in Your Mouth Could Be Destiny
ei.subject: 10월_2025 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Chemistry in Your Mouth Could Be Destiny

fullPassage: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. Then, gargle with water to thoroughly clean your tongue, use a swab coated with sugar on the same spots, and record those results. Gargle again, and then swab with lemon juice. After a final gargle, try coffee. Compare your reactions with your friends'. Your taste pattern may reveal more than just taste preferences. Recent studies suggest links between taster status and behavioral disorders. For example, "non-tasters" tend to have a higher incidence of alcoholism, perhaps because liquor seems less bitter to them. Conversely, "super-tasters" may avoid nutritious but mildly bitter foods such as broccoli, thus depriving themselves of a balanced diet. So, although taste is not nearly as glamorous as vision, hearing, or even touch, it makes sense for you to pay closer attention to it because chemistry, at least in your mouth, could be destiny.

❌ ② strongest — 원문 일치. '맛이 가장 강하게(strongest) 느껴지는 곳'에 적절
❌ ③ thoroughly — 원문 일치. '혀를 완전히(thoroughly) 깨끗이 닦는다'에 적절
❌ ④ bitter — 원문 일치. '술이 덜 쓰게(bitter) 느껴진다'에 적절

✅ ④ less — 원문 closer(더 가까이). less(덜)로 바꾸면 '미각에 덜 주의를 기울여야 한다'가 되어 글 전체 주장과 정반대 ←정답

✅ ③ providing(제공하는): depriving(빼앗는)의 반의어. 빼앗는 것과 제공하는 것은 정반대 ←정답
❌ ④ exhausting(지치게 하는): 에너지 소모와 관련된 다른 의미 축
det.tip: depriving themselves of a balanced diet — 균형 잡힌 식단을 스스로에게서 빼앗다

questions.passage:
(A) It makes <u>sense</u> for you to pay closer attention to your diet.
(B) Dogs have a keen <u>sense</u> of smell that far surpasses humans.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 sense가 뜻하는 바로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은? (A) (B)

det.korean: (A) make sense=이치에 맞다, 타당하다 (B) sense of smell=후각(감각)
det.analysis:
❌ ① 의미 — 감각: (A) make sense는 '의미가 있다'보다 '이치에 맞다/타당하다'가 정확
✅ ② 이치 — 감각: (A) 'it makes sense'=이치에 맞다 (B) 'sense of smell'=후각(감각) ←정답
❌ ③ 이치 — 방향: (B) sense of smell은 '방향'이 아닌 '감각'
❌ ④ 감각 — 의미: (A) make sense는 '감각'이 아닌 '이치', (B)는 '의미'가 아닌 '감각'
det.tip: (A) it makes sense = 이치에 맞다 / (B) sense of smell = 후각(감각)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"the rate at which something happens, especially something unpleasant"

det.analysis:
❌ ① tendency(경향): 발생률이 아닌 성향/경향
✅ ② incidence(발생률): '특히 불쾌한 일이 발생하는 비율'이라는 정의에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ influence(영향): 발생률이 아닌 영향력
❌ ④ frequency(빈도): 유사하지만 '특히 불쾌한 것'이라는 한정이 없음
det.tip: a higher incidence of alcoholism — 알코올 중독의 더 높은 발생률

questions.passage: Recent studies suggest links between taster status and __________ (behave) disorders.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 명사 disorders를 수식하는 형용사가 필요하다. 동사 behave의 명사형 behavior에 접미사 -al을 붙여 형용사 behavioral(행동의, 행동과 관련된)이 된다. 영국식 behavioural도 정답으로 인정.
det.tip: behave(동사) → behavior(명사) → behavioral(형용사)

questions.passage: Conversely, "super-tasters" may avoid __________ (nutrition) but mildly bitter foods such as broccoli, thus depriving themselves of a balanced diet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 빈칸 뒤의 'but mildly bitter foods'에서 foods를 수식하는 형용사가 필요하다. 명사 nutrition(영양)에서 형용사 nutritious(영양가 있는)로 변환한다. 'nutritious but mildly bitter foods'=영양가 있지만 약간 쓴 음식.
det.tip: nutrition(명사) → nutritious(형용사: 영양가 있는)

questions.passage: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. Then, gargle with water to thoroughly clean your tongue, use a swab coated with sugar on the same spots, and record those results. Gargle again, and then swab with lemon juice. After a final gargle, try coffee. Compare your reactions with your friends'. Your taste pattern may reveal more than just __________. Recent studies suggest links between taster status and behavioral disorders. For example, "non-tasters" tend to have a higher incidence of alcoholism, perhaps because liquor seems less bitter to them. Conversely, "super-tasters" may avoid nutritious but mildly bitter foods such as broccoli, thus depriving themselves of a balanced diet. So, although taste is not nearly as glamorous as vision, hearing, or even touch, it makes sense for you to pay closer attention to it because chemistry, at least in your mouth, could be destiny.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '단순한 ~ 이상의 것을 드러낸다'의 빈칸. taste preferences=맛 선호
det.analysis:
❌ ① eating habits(식습관): 맛 패턴과 유사하지만 원문은 taste preferences 표현 사용
❌ ② health conditions(건강 상태): 맛 선호보다 범위가 넓어 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ cooking methods(조리법): 조리법과 무관한 맥락
✅ ④ taste preferences(맛 선호): 맛 패턴이 단순한 맛 선호 이상의 것, 즉 행동 장애와의 연관성까지 드러낸다는 원문 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: more than just __________ — 단순한 맛 선호 이상의 것

questions.passage: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. Then, gargle with water to thoroughly clean your tongue, use a swab coated with sugar on the same spots, and record those results. Gargle again, and then swab with lemon juice. After a final gargle, try coffee. Compare your reactions with your friends'. Your taste pattern may reveal more than just taste preferences. Recent studies suggest links between taster status and behavioral disorders. For example, "non-tasters" tend to have a higher incidence of alcoholism, perhaps because liquor seems less bitter to them. Conversely, "super-tasters" may avoid nutritious but mildly bitter foods such as broccoli, thus depriving themselves of a balanced diet. So, although taste is not nearly as glamorous as vision, hearing, or even touch, it makes sense for you to pay closer attention to it because chemistry, at least in your mouth, __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '입 안의 화학작용은 ~'의 빈칸. could be destiny=운명이 될 수 있다
det.analysis:
✅ ① could be destiny(운명이 될 수 있다): 미각이 행동과 식습관에 영향을 미쳐 운명이 될 수 있다는 글의 결론 ←정답
❌ ② remains a mystery(여전히 미스터리다): 연구 결과를 근거로 제시했으므로 미스터리가 아님
❌ ③ is purely genetic(순전히 유전적이다): 유전에 대한 논의 없음
❌ ④ has no significance(의미가 없다): 미각의 중요성을 강조하는 글의 논지와 정반대
det.tip: chemistry, at least in your mouth, __________ — 입 안의 화학작용은 운명이 될 수 있다
